find: “a shaven-headed full moon” — The metaphor compares the grandfather’s shaved head to the moon. This is a moment of tender, personal memory in a poem about national ideology. The grandfather represents the human life that the pilot is being asked to throw away.
replace: “a shaven head / full of powerful incantations” — The pilot’s head is “full” of ritual chants, not of his own thoughts. He has been filled up with other people’s beliefs. Later the poem turns to tender, personal memory — waiting on the shore for “grandfather’s boat” — and that ordinary human life is what the pilot is being asked to throw away.
note: F18: 'a shaven-headed full moon' is not in the poem; the text reads 'a shaven head / full of powerful incantations', and it is the pilot's head, not the grandfather's.
